Uttar Pradesh Ration Card & 
Public Distribution System 
The Complete Reference: Law, Eligibility, Documents, Certificates, Application Process, Digital 
Systems, Procurement, Grievances & Facts/Figures 
Compiled as a knowledge-base / dataset-training reference for the Public Distribution Scheme (Ration) and 
Welfare Scheme project 
Scope: Uttar Pradesh only. Official portals referenced: fcs.up.gov.in, edistrict.up.gov.in (esathi.up.gov.in), familyid.up.gov.in, 
nfsa.up.gov.in, dfpd.gov.in, fci.gov.in 
All facts and figures in this document are drawn from published government sources (PIB, DFPD, FCI, Economic Survey, PRS Legislative 
Research) and reputable secondary guides, with sources cited at the end of each section. Where a specific UP-level statistic is not publicly 
available in verifiable form, this document says so explicitly rather than estimating.
Table of Contents

1. Introduction 
A Ration Card in Uttar Pradesh is an official document issued by the Department of Food & Civil Supplies 
(Khadya Evam Rasad Vibhag) that entitles eligible households to buy subsidised — and since January 2023, 
largely free — food grains (wheat, rice, and coarse grains/millets) from Fair Price Shops (FPS) under the National 
Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013. Uttar Pradesh operates one of the largest Public Distribution Systems (PDS) in 
the country. 
According to figures compiled from the FCS UP portal and secondary aggregators, Uttar Pradesh has over 3.6 
crore ration cards covering around 14.6 crore beneficiaries, distributed through more than 80,000 Fair Price 
Shops spread across all 75 districts of the state. This makes UP's PDS network the largest of any single state in 
India by beneficiary count. 
Beyond food subsidy, the ration card doubles as a supporting identity and address-proof document accepted for 
several other government services, and — together with the Family ID (Ek Parivar Ek Pehchan) — acts as an 
entry point into the wider welfare ecosystem in UP, including pension schemes, scholarships, and schemes such 
as Kanya Sumangala Yojana. 
Source: fcs.up.gov.in aggregated via CitizenNest and India Customer Care guides 
2. History & Evolution of the Ration Card System 
2.1 Origins in India 
Rationing in India traces back to World War II-era food scarcity in the 1940s, when the colonial government 
introduced grain rationing in select cities. After independence, the system was gradually expanded and 
formalised into the Public Distribution System (PDS), which for decades operated as a general entitlement 
scheme without strict income-based targeting. 
2.2 Shift to Targeted PDS (1997) 
In June 1997, the Government of India launched the Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS), which for the 
first time distinguished Below Poverty Line (BPL) and Above Poverty Line (APL) households, aiming to direct 
subsidies more specifically toward poorer households rather than the population at large. 
2.3 Antyodaya Anna Yojana (2000) 
On 25 December 2000, the Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) was launched as a special sub-scheme within TPDS to 
identify and support the 'poorest of the poor' — households such as those headed by widows, disabled persons, 
elderly people without support, and other highly vulnerable groups — with a larger, low-cost monthly foodgrain 
entitlement. 
2.4 National Food Security Act, 2013 
The National Food Security Act (NFSA), also called the Right to Food Act, was passed by Parliament on 5 July 
2013 (signed into law 12 September 2013, retroactively effective from 5 July 2013) under the UPA government 
led by Prime Minister Manmohan Singh. This converted food subsidy from a discretionary welfare scheme into a 
legal entitlement for eligible households, covering PDS, the midday meal scheme, and maternity entitlements 
under one umbrella law. 
2.5 Digitisation Era (2014 onward)

From the mid-2010s, states including Uttar Pradesh progressively digitised ration card databases, seeded 
Aadhaar numbers against beneficiary records, and rolled out electronic Point of Sale (e-PoS) devices at Fair Price 
Shops for biometric authentication — aimed at removing duplicate/bogus cards ('ghost beneficiaries') and 
improving last-mile delivery accuracy. 
2.6 COVID-19 and PMGKAY (2020–2023) 
The Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) was launched on 26 March 2020 in response to the 
COVID-19 pandemic, initially providing an additional 5 kg of free foodgrain and 1 kg of pulses per person per 
month, on top of regular NFSA entitlements, to roughly 80 crore beneficiaries nationwide. It was extended in 
phases through 2020–2022. 
2.7 Integration of PMGKAY into NFSA (2023–2028) 
From 1 January 2023, the government merged PMGKAY into NFSA and began providing the standard NFSA 
entitlement (5 kg/person/month for Priority Households, 35 kg/household/month for AAY) completely free of 
cost, rather than at the earlier subsidised prices of Rs. 1–3/kg. This arrangement has since been extended for a 
further five years, through December 2028. 
2.8 One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC) 
ONORC, rolled out nationally by mid-2020s, allows any NFSA cardholder to draw their entitlement from any Fair 
Price Shop in the country using Aadhaar-based biometric or OTP authentication, benefiting migrant workers in 
particular. Uttar Pradesh, both as a large source state for migrant labour and a destination state, is a full 
participant in ONORC. 
Source: Business Standard; PubAdmin Institute; PMFIAS; Grokipedia summary of NFSA, 2013; DFPD notifications

3. Legal Framework: National Food Security Act, 2013 
The NFSA is the central law underpinning ration card entitlements everywhere in India, including Uttar Pradesh. 
Key provisions relevant to beneficiaries: 
• 
Coverage: up to 75% of the rural population and up to 50% of the urban population are legally entitled 
to subsidised/free foodgrains — together, about two-thirds of India's population nationally. 
• 
Two beneficiary categories: Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) households (poorest of the poor) and Priority 
Households (PHH), identified by state governments using prescribed criteria. 
• 
Entitlement quantities: AAY households get 35 kg of foodgrain per household per month; PHH 
beneficiaries get 5 kg per person per month. 
• 
Legislated prices (pre-2023): not exceeding Rs. 3/kg for rice, Rs. 2/kg for wheat, and Rs. 1/kg for coarse 
grains — foodgrains have been provided free of cost since January 2023 under the PMGKAY–NFSA 
merger. 
• 
Women's empowerment provision: the eldest woman of the household, aged 18 years or above, is to be 
recognised as the head of household for the purpose of issuing the ration card, unless no adult woman is 
available. 
• 
Food Security Allowance: if entitled foodgrains are not supplied to a beneficiary in a given month, the 
State Government is legally required to pay a Food Security Allowance, under the Food Security 
Allowance Rules, 2015. 
• 
Grievance redressal: every district is required to have a District Grievance Redressal Officer (DGRO) 
empowered to hear PDS-related complaints, alongside State Food Commissions constituted under the 
Act. 
• 
Transparency provisions: PDS-related records (allocation, offtake, FPS-wise beneficiary lists) are required 
to be disclosed publicly — this is the legal basis for the eligibility lists published on fcs.up.gov.in and 
nfsa.up.gov.in. 
• 
Decentralised procurement: the Act permits state governments/agencies to procure, store, and 
distribute foodgrains within the state directly (with central government reimbursement), rather than 
relying solely on central pool stocks routed through the Food Corporation of India (FCI). 
Source: dfpd.gov.in — National Food Security Act, 2013 (Act No. 20 of 2013); PRS Legislative Research; PMFIAS

5. Eligibility Criteria (Detailed) 
5.1 General eligibility to apply 
• 
Must be a permanent resident of Uttar Pradesh with valid address proof in the state. 
• 
Must be at least 18 years old to apply as head of the family. 
• 
The family must not already hold a valid ration card anywhere else in India. 
• 
Annual family income must be below the state-prescribed limit — commonly cited as up to Rs. 2 
lakh/year for rural households and Rs. 3 lakh/year for urban households (these limits are set/revised by 
the state government; always confirm the current limit on fcs.up.gov.in). 
• 
Newly married couples without an existing card, and holders of expired/temporary cards, can apply for a 
fresh regular card. 
5.2 AAY-specific eligibility (poorest-of-the-poor priority) 
• 
Households headed by widows, disabled persons, or persons aged 60 years or more with no assured 
means of subsistence or societal support. 
• 
Primitive tribal households, and households with no regular source of income. 
• 
Landless agricultural labourers, marginal farmers, rickshaw pullers, hand-cart pullers, cobblers, and 
similarly placed casual/informal workers, per broader central AAY guidelines adopted by states. 
5.3 Exclusion criteria (commonly applied) 
• 
Income-tax payers or professional-tax payers in the household. 
• 
Government employees above certain grade levels. 
• 
Owners of four-wheeler motor vehicles (excluding those used commercially, per some state guidelines). 
• 
Households already covered under a ration card in another state (until surrendered). 
Note: Exact income limits and exclusion criteria are revised periodically by the state government; the figures above reflect 
commonly cited thresholds in recent secondary reporting and should be reconfirmed on fcs.up.gov.in before an application is 
filed. 
Source: India Customer Care; CitizenNest guides

6.1 Aadhaar Card 
Aadhaar, issued by UIDAI, is the base identity document for nearly every step of the ration card process — 
application, e-KYC, and biometric authentication at the Fair Price Shop. 
1. Locate your nearest Aadhaar Seva Kendra or bank-based enrolment centre.

2. Carry an existing ID/address proof (birth certificate, school ID, existing ration card, etc.) for first-time 
enrolment. 
3. Complete biometric capture (fingerprints, iris, photograph) at the centre. 
4. Aadhaar is generated and posted, and is also downloadable from uidai.gov.in once ready. 
Updating Aadhaar details 
Name, address, date of birth, or mobile number can be updated online (for some fields) or at an Aadhaar Seva 
Kendra. Address updates in particular are relevant before a ration card application, since the e-KYC pulls the 
address on record. 
Source: UIDAI general enrolment guidance 
6.2 Family ID (Ek Parivar Ek Pehchan) 
The UP Family ID is a unique 12-digit identification number assigned to each household, consolidating family 
details for streamlined access to ration cards, pensions, scholarships, and other welfare schemes. If your family 
already holds a ration card, the card number itself typically becomes/links to the Family ID; households without 
a ration card register fresh. 
How to apply 
5. Visit familyid.up.gov.in and select New Registration. 
6. Choose 'Ration Card holder' if you already have a ration card (the system pulls existing family data), or 
'Naya Pehchan' (New Identity) if you do not. 
7. Enter the head of family's Aadhaar number and verify via OTP sent to the Aadhaar-linked mobile 
number. 
8. Fill in details of all family members and submit. 
Note: Processing is largely instant to a few days depending on data-matching accuracy. There is no fee for Family ID 
registration. 
Source: egovtschemes.com; pppfamilyiid.com — UP Family ID guides 
6.3 Income Certificate (Aay Praman Patra) 
Issued by the Revenue Department through the local Tehsildar; certifies the applicant/family's income from all 
sources. Commonly needed for PHH/AAY ration card category applications, plus scholarships and other subsidy 
schemes. Valid for 3 years in UP. 
Documents needed to obtain it 
• 
Aadhaar card (mandatory e-KYC — name and photo auto-fill from UIDAI) 
• 
Self-Declaration Form (Swaprashit Ghoshna Patra) stating total annual family income, downloadable 
from the eSathi portal footer 
• 
Proof of address 
• 
Recent photograph (or use the Aadhaar photo option) 
How to apply (online, via eSathi) 
9. Go to edistrict.up.gov.in and click Citizen Login (redirects to esathi.up.gov.in); new users click New User 
Registration. 
10. After logging in, choose Apply for Certificate → Income Certificate (Aay Praman Patra).

11. Select Rural (Gramin) or Urban (Nagariya) based on actual residence — this decides who verifies the 
application. 
12. Fill personal details, upload documents (PDF/JPEG, generally under ~100 KB each), and submit. 
13. Field verification is carried out by the Lekhpal (rural) or Revenue Inspector (urban) before the Tehsildar 
digitally signs and issues the certificate. 
14. Track status online using the application number, and download the signed certificate once approved. 
Note: Offline option: collect/print the form at your nearest Tehsil office, fill it, attach documents, and submit at the counter. 
CSC operators may charge an additional Rs. 30–50 service fee. 
Source: India Customer Care; edistrictup.in 
6.4 Domicile / Residence Certificate (Niwas Praman Patra) 
UP recognises two variants: Samanya Niwas Praman Patra (Ordinary Residence Certificate — current address) 
and Mool Niwas Praman Patra (Permanent/Original Domicile Certificate — ancestral/permanent UP residence). 
The latter is generally required for state-quota admissions, government job applications, and certain welfare 
scheme linkages. 
Eligibility 
• 
3 years of continuous residence in Uttar Pradesh, OR 
• 
Born in UP, or parents are permanent UP residents (qualifies regardless of the applicant's own residence 
duration) 
Documents required 
• 
Proof of identity (Aadhaar, Voter ID, Passport, etc.) 
• 
Proof of address (ration card, utility bills, bank passbook, rent agreement) 
• 
Proof of long-term stay (school certificates, property documents, older utility bills) 
• 
Family ID (mandatory on the eSathi portal) 
• 
Self-declaration affidavit of residence 
How to apply 
15. Visit edistrict.up.gov.in (via esathi.up.gov.in), log in, and select Domicile Certificate under Apply for 
Certificate. 
16. Select Rural or Urban, and enter your Family ID. 
17. Fill personal and residence-history details and upload supporting documents. 
18. Field verification by the Lekhpal/Revenue Inspector, followed by issue from the Tehsildar's office — 
typically within about 30 days. 
Source: India Customer Care; LegalRaasta — UP Domicile Certificate guides 
6.5 Caste Certificate (Jati Praman Patra) 
Needed only where reserved-category benefits are being claimed alongside ration/welfare entitlements. Issued 
by the Tehsildar/SDM/ADM. 
• 
Address proof: Aadhaar, ration card, voter ID, or utility bill 
• 
Identity proof: Aadhaar, PAN, or voter ID 
• 
Self-declaration certificate

• 
Recent photograph 
• 
Income certificate (for OBC/non-creamy-layer claims) 
Online application is generally routed through edistrict.up.gov.in; where online filing isn't available for a 
particular caste category, applicants submit the form with a Rs. 1.50 court-fee stamp at the local Tehsil office or 
CSC. 
Source: LegalRaasta — UP Caste Certificate guide 
6.6 Disability Certificate (for AAY priority classification) 
For households where a disabled member is the basis for AAY (poorest-of-the-poor) classification, a disability 
certificate issued by the Chief Medical Officer (CMO) or a district hospital medical board is typically required 
alongside standard identity/address documents. 
• 
Application at the CMO office or notified district hospital 
• 
Medical board assessment and disability percentage certification 
• 
Aadhaar and photograph required alongside the medical assessment form 
Source: General Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 certification framework as applied at district level 
6.7 Death, Birth & Marriage Certificates (for card updates) 
These civil registration documents are frequently needed when updating an existing ration card rather than for a 
fresh application: 
• 
Death Certificate — required to remove a deceased member from the card. Apply via edistrict.up.gov.in 
(Nagar Nigam/Nagar Palika for urban, Gram Panchayat for rural registration). 
• 
Birth Certificate — required to add a newborn to the family's card. Registration is done with the local 
municipal body or Gram Panchayat, typically within 21 days of birth for the simplest process. 
• 
Marriage Certificate — supports splitting a household into a new, separate ration card for a newly 
married couple; can be obtained via the Sub-Registrar's office or edistrict.up.gov.in's marriage 
registration service. 
Source: edistrict.up.gov.in civil registration services — general guidance

7. Step-by-Step: How to Apply for a New Ration Card 
7.1 Online Application (fcs.up.gov.in) 
19. Go to the official portal: fcs.up.gov.in. 
20. Register using your mobile number if you're a new user, and create your login. 
21. Look for 'नवीन राशन कार्ड के लिए आवेदन' (Apply for New Ration Card) on the homepage. 
22. Fill the application form: head of family details, all family members with Aadhaar numbers, address, 
LPG/electricity connection details, income, and bank information. 
23. Upload the required documents (JPG/PDF, usually under ~200 KB per file). 
24. Review all entered details carefully, then submit the form. 
25. Note down the application Reference ID / Sandarbh ID shown on the acknowledgement — needed to 
track status later. 
Note: There is no government fee for a new ration card. If anyone demands payment beyond the standard CSC service 
charge, it may be fraudulent — report it via the helplines in Section 14. 
Source: CitizenNest; India Customer Care — application steps 
7.2 Offline Application (CSC / Tehsil Supply Office) 
26. Visit your nearest Common Service Centre (CSC/Jan Seva Kendra) or the Tehsil (Block) Supply Office. 
27. The CSC operator logs into the e-District/FCS system on your behalf and fills the form, or you collect and 
fill a printed form (separate formats for rural/urban applicants). 
28. Submit the filled form with self-attested photocopies of all required documents. 
29. Collect the acknowledgement slip bearing your Reference ID. 
30. A Supply Inspector (आपूलतड लनरीक्षक) — via the Gram Panchayat Officer in rural areas — carries out field 
verification, typically within 15–30 days. 
31. After verification and approval, your name is added to the NFSA eligibility list and the ration card is 
issued. 
Source: India Customer Care; Tribune India — offline application steps 
7.3 Field Verification Process (What Happens Behind the Scenes) 
Once an application is submitted (online or offline), it is routed to the local revenue/supply hierarchy for 
physical verification before approval: 
• 
Rural areas: the Gram Panchayat Officer/Lekhpal verifies household details, income claims, and 
residence, often visiting the address in person. 
• 
Urban areas: a Revenue Inspector/Supply Inspector conducts the equivalent verification for households 
within municipal limits. 
• 
Verification typically checks: actual residence at the stated address, family composition against 
Aadhaar/Family ID records, absence of an existing ration card elsewhere, and rough consistency of the 
income claim with visible household circumstances. 
• 
The verifying officer submits a report/recommendation to the District Supply Officer (DSO), who 
approves or rejects the application and assigns the card category (AAY/PHH/EHH). 
Source: Compiled from CitizenNest and India Customer Care process descriptions

7.4 Checking Application Status 
32. Go to fcs.up.gov.in. 
33. Click 'राशन कार्ड आवेदन की स्थिलत' (Ration Card Application Status) under Important Links. 
34. Enter your Ration ID / Reference ID / Sandarbh ID and the captcha code. 
35. Click 'Get OTP', enter the OTP received on your registered mobile number, and submit. 
36. Your current status is displayed on screen. 
Source: Sarkari Yojana — FCS UP status check steps 
7.5 Ration Card Eligibility List / Downloading the Card 
Once approved, you can view/search your entry and download the card in a few ways: 
• 
FCS Portal: fcs.up.gov.in → 'राशन कार्ड की पात्रता सूची' → select District → Block/Town → Gram 
Panchayat/Ward → Fair Price Shop dealer to see the full beneficiary list, or search directly by ration card 
number with OTP verification. 
• 
DigiLocker: Open the DigiLocker app or digilocker.gov.in, log in with your Aadhaar-linked mobile 
number, search 'Ration Card', select the issuing department, and fetch the document. 
• 
Mera Ration 2.0 App: Available on Play Store/App Store; log in with Aadhaar-based authentication to 
view/download your card and check entitlements — useful under ONORC. 
Source: Bajaj Finserv; India Customer Care — ration card download methods

9. Managing an Existing Ration Card 
9.1 Adding a family member 
37. Log in at fcs.up.gov.in → Modification section → 'Add Member'. 
38. Enter the new member's details and Aadhaar number. 
39. Attach supporting document (e.g., birth certificate for a newborn, marriage certificate for a spouse). 
40. Submit for verification by the Supply Inspector. 
9.2 Removing a member 
41. Use the 'Delete Member' option on the same portal. 
42. Attach supporting proof — typically a death certificate, or proof of the member's inclusion on a separate 
new household card. 
9.3 Corrections (name, address, category) 
Apply through the correction/modification link on fcs.up.gov.in, or at the Tehsil Supply Office, with supporting 
documents proving the correct detail (e.g., Aadhaar for name spelling). 
9.4 Renewal, duplicate card & surrender 
• 
Renewal: use the renewal form on fcs.up.gov.in or edistrict.up.gov.in when a card nears expiry or needs 
reissue. 
• 
Duplicate/lost card: apply for a duplicate at the Tehsil Supply Office or online, typically with an 
FIR/police report reference if the original was lost or stolen, plus identity proof.

• 
Surrender: required before permanently moving to another state (to avoid duplicate-card violations), or 
when a household is being merged/split. 
Source: CitizenNest — UP Ration Card modification steps 
10. Digital Systems: e-PoS, Aadhaar Seeding & ONORC 
10.1 Electronic Point of Sale (e-PoS) 
Fair Price Shops in UP use e-PoS devices that authenticate beneficiaries biometrically (fingerprint/iris) or via OTP 
before dispensing foodgrain, and log the transaction quantity electronically against the beneficiary's Aadhaarseeded ration card. UP has also linked e-PoS machines with electronic weighing scales, an initiative highlighted 
at the national level for improving delivery accuracy of the exact entitled quantity. 
10.2 Aadhaar Seeding 
Aadhaar seeding — linking each beneficiary's Aadhaar number to their ration card entry — is mandatory 
nationwide, including in UP, to prevent duplicate/ghost beneficiaries and to enable biometric authentication at 
the FPS. 
10.3 One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC) 
ONORC allows ration cardholders to draw their entitlement from any Fair Price Shop in India using Aadhaarbased authentication. Nationally, during 2024, roughly 30 crore portability transactions were recorded over 11 
months, delivering around 66 lakh metric tonnes (LMT) of foodgrain through inter-state and intra-state 
portability under NFSA and PMGKAY combined — with more than 2.5 crore portability transactions recorded per 
month under PMGKAY foodgrain distribution specifically. Uttar Pradesh, as both a major source state for 
migrant labour and a large PDS state, participates fully in ONORC. 
10.4 Mera Ration 2.0 App & DigiLocker 
The Mera Ration 2.0 mobile app (Play Store/App Store) and DigiLocker allow Aadhaar-authenticated cardholders 
to view entitlements, locate nearby Fair Price Shops, and download a digital copy of the ration card without 
visiting an office. 
Source: PIB — Year-End Review of Department of Food and Public Distribution, 2024 (ONORC transaction volumes); PIB/news reports on 
UP e-PoS–weighing scale integration

11. Procurement & Supply Chain Behind the PDS 
11.1 Minimum Support Price (MSP) & Procurement 
Before foodgrain reaches Fair Price Shops, it must first be procured from farmers at the Minimum Support Price 
(MSP) — a floor price set by the Central Government each season to protect farmer incomes — and 
stored/transported through the Food Corporation of India (FCI) and, in some states, state procurement agencies 
under decentralised procurement. 
Verified procurement figures 
• 
Rabi Marketing Season (RMS) 2024-25: total wheat procurement across India reached about 266 Lakh 
Metric Tonnes (LMT), up from 262 LMT in RMS 2023-24 and 188 LMT in RMS 2022-23. 
• 
Uttar Pradesh's wheat procurement in RMS 2024-25 was reported at approximately 9.31 LMT (an 
interim government release) — a sharp rise from about 2.20 LMT in the previous season — with a 
separate mid-season figure citing 9.07 LMT as of late May 2024; both figures come from official 
Consumer Affairs Ministry updates at different points in the procurement window, and reflect UP's 
traditionally modest share of central-pool wheat procurement compared to Punjab, Haryana, and 
Madhya Pradesh. 
• 
MSP for wheat, RMS 2024-25: Rs. 2,275 per quintal, benefiting more than 22 lakh farmers nationally 
with about Rs. 61,000 crore credited directly to farmer bank accounts. 
• 
Kharif Marketing Season 2023-24 (national): paddy procurement exceeded 728 LMT, equivalent to 
about 489.15 LMT of milled rice, from around 98.26 lakh farmers, with an MSP outflow of roughly Rs. 
1,60,000 crore. 
• 
Production context (Economic Survey 2025-26, 2024-25 crop year): Uttar Pradesh is India's largest 
wheat-producing state, with 35.65 million tonnes (about 30.2% of national wheat production), and the 
largest rice-producing state, with 20.76 million tonnes (about 13.8% of national rice production). 
Note: UP's large production base does not automatically translate into large central-pool procurement volumes — much of 
UP's wheat and rice moves through open-market and local trade channels rather than government procurement, which is 
why its MSP procurement figures are modest relative to Punjab/Haryana despite leading national production. 
Source: PIB press releases on RMS 2024-25 wheat procurement; Business Standard, Business Today, NewsOnAir coverage of the same 
government release; Economic Survey 2025-26 Statistical Appendix (Table 1.18) 
11.2 Central Issue Price (CIP) & Economic Cost 
The Central Issue Price is the rate at which the Centre supplies foodgrain to states for PDS distribution; the 
difference between CIP and the government's actual economic cost of handling grain is borne as food subsidy. 
• 
In 2002-03 (when CIP first became effective), the economic cost of rice was about Rs. 11.7/kg and wheat 
about Rs. 8.8/kg. 
• 
By 2024-25 (estimated), the economic cost had risen to about Rs. 39.8/kg for rice and Rs. 27.7/kg for 
wheat — reflecting storage, transport, and procurement cost inflation over two decades. 
• 
Since foodgrain is now supplied free to NFSA beneficiaries, nearly the entire economic cost is absorbed 
as central food subsidy. 
Source: PRS Legislative Research — Demand for Grants 2024-25 Analysis: Food and Public Distribution 
11.3 Storage, Transit & Losses

Foodgrain moves from procurement centres to FCI/state godowns, then onward to Fair Price Shops via a districtlevel supply chain. Some loss occurs in storage and transit, tracked and reported by FCI for accountability. 
• 
At the national level, FCI has been increasing use of containerised rail ('rakes') and multi-modal 
transport (coastal shipping plus road) to cut freight costs and transit time, including inter-state 
movement relevant to UP's supply chain as both a producing and consuming state. 
• 
During 2024 (January–October), FCI moved a total of 10,205 rakes of foodgrain, amounting to 
approximately 358.93 LMT, nationally. 
Source: PIB — Year-End Review of Department of Food and Public Distribution, 2024 
12. Fair Price Shop (FPS) System 
12.1 Dealer appointment & margins 
Fair Price Shop dealers are appointed by the district administration (District Supply Officer) under state PDS 
control order rules, typically preferring cooperative societies, self-help groups, or individuals meeting eligibility 
norms set by the state. Dealers earn a commission/margin per quintal of foodgrain sold, partly reimbursed by 
the central government under NFSA. 
12.2 Vigilance & monitoring 
• 
Vigilance Committees at the Fair Price Shop, block, and district levels are meant to include local citizen 
representatives to monitor stock arrival, distribution, and pricing at FPS outlets. 
• 
e-PoS transaction logs create a digital audit trail that supply departments and vigilance authorities can 
cross-check against physical stock registers. 
• 
Common malpractices flagged historically include short-weighing, diversion of stock to the open market, 
and inclusion of ineligible ('bogus') beneficiaries — these are precisely the issues Aadhaar seeding and ePoS digitisation are designed to reduce. 
12.3 Reporting problems at an FPS 
Beneficiaries facing short-weighing, denial of entitlement, or dealer misconduct can complain via the toll-free 
helpline, the fcs.up.gov.in grievance section, or in person to the District Supply Officer (see Section 14). 
Source: General PDS control order framework as reported across state PDS guidance and government vigilance mechanisms

14.1 Escalation sequence for a stuck application 
43. Check status online at fcs.up.gov.in using the Reference ID. 
44. If unresolved beyond the normal 15–30 day window, call the toll-free helpline (1967 / 1800-1800-150). 
45. File an online grievance at fcs.up.gov.in and/or CPGRAMS (pgportal.gov.in) — Department of Food & 
Public Distribution. 
46. If still unresolved, file an RTI request under the RTI Act, 2005, addressed to the District Supply Officer 
and/or Tehsil Food Inspector, requesting the verification report and current file status. 
47. A First Appeal under Section 19(1) of the RTI Act can follow if the RTI response is silent or evasive, and a 
Second Appeal to the State Information Commission thereafter.

15. Related UP Welfare Schemes Linked via Ration Card / Family ID 
Because the ration card and Family ID are used as base identity/eligibility layers for several other UP welfare 
programmes, applicants working on a broader PDS/welfare chatbot may also want to track these adjoining 
schemes: 
• 
Pension Schemes (old-age, widow, disability pensions) — often cross-verified against ration card/Family 
ID data for eligibility and duplicate-beneficiary checks. 
• 
Kanya Sumangala Yojana — a girl-child welfare scheme in UP where family income and Family ID/ration 
card records may be used as supporting eligibility documentation.

• 
Scholarship schemes (pre-matric/post-matric, OBC/SC/ST) — income and caste certificates obtained via 
the same edistrict.up.gov.in workflow described in Section 6 are commonly reused here. 
Note: This document's core focus remains the ration card/PDS system; the above is included only as cross-reference context 
relevant to the wider Public Distribution Scheme (Ration) and Welfare Scheme project.

17. Comprehensive FAQ 
Is there any fee for a new ration card? 
No government fee for issuance itself. CSC/Jan Seva Kendra may charge a nominal service fee (roughly Rs. 10–
30). 
How long does it take to get a ration card? 
Typically 15–30 days after submission, including field verification, though actual timelines can vary by district. 
Can I apply if I already have a ration card in another state? 
No — a household can hold only one active ration card in India. You must surrender the old card before/while 
applying fresh in UP. 
Is Aadhaar mandatory? 
Yes, for the head of family at minimum, and generally for all members being added, for e-KYC and biometric 
authentication at the Fair Price Shop. 
What if my income certificate application is rejected or delayed? 
Check the reason on the eSathi status page; common causes are mismatched Aadhaar e-KYC details or 
incomplete self-declaration. Reapply after correcting the flagged issue, or visit the Tehsil office directly. 
Is foodgrain really free now, or subsidised? 
Since 1 January 2023, NFSA foodgrain (5 kg/person for PHH, 35 kg/household for AAY) is provided completely 
free of cost under the PMGKAY–NFSA merger, extended through December 2028. 
What is the difference between Samanya Niwas Praman Patra and Mool Niwas Praman Patra? 
Samanya Niwas Praman Patra proves your current residential address; Mool Niwas Praman Patra proves 
permanent/ancestral domicile in UP and is generally what's needed for state-quota admissions and government 
jobs. 
Can a migrant worker from UP use their ration card outside the state? 
Yes, under ONORC, a UP ration card can be used at any Fair Price Shop in India with Aadhaar-based 
authentication, without needing to apply for a new card in the destination state. 
What happens if the Fair Price Shop dealer gives less quantity than entitled? 
This is a reportable violation — complain via the toll-free helpline (1967 / 1800-1800-150) or the fcs.up.gov.in 
grievance section; under NFSA, a Food Security Allowance may also be payable if entitlement isn't supplied. 
Does the ration card expire? 
Cards can need renewal/reissue over time (e.g., damaged card, long-unused card flagged in periodic verification 
drives); use the renewal option on fcs.up.gov.in or edistrict.up.gov.in when required. 
Who decides whether a household gets AAY or PHH classification? 
The District Supply Officer, based on the field verification report from the Lekhpal/Supply Inspector and the 
eligibility criteria set by the state (income, vulnerability indicators such as disability/widowhood/old age, and 
NFSA quotas). 
Can women apply as head of household?

Yes — NFSA specifically provides that the eldest woman of the household, aged 18 or above, is to be recognised 
as the head of household for ration card issuance, unless no adult woman is available in the family. 
What is the role of the Family ID in the ration card process? 
Family ID consolidates household data across schemes; many certificate applications (e.g., Domicile Certificate) 
now mandate entering the Family ID, and it can also link the household to other welfare schemes beyond PDS. 
Is there a helpline specifically for senior citizens or SC/ST grievances related to welfare schemes? 
Yes, at the national level there are dedicated helplines such as the National Helpline for Senior Citizens 
(14567/Elderline) and the SC/ST Atrocities Prevention National Helpline (14566), alongside the general PDS 
helpline for ration-specific issues.
